newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - Nov 18.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Deferred payment consumer good imports on sharp rise, reaching $5.08 billion during the first nine months.
- Government and ruling New Korea Party weigh plan to select education superintendents through direct popular election.

- China is responsive to four-way talks on Korean peninsula peace regime, and will take part in the talks pending an agreement by other related countries:, according to the Chinese ambassador to Seoul.
- Mid-level government officials without commensurate portfolios number more than 1,000, running contrary to the current administration's pledge to shrink the government.
- The United States is unhappy with the South Korean administration under President Kim Young-sam, who has turned hawkish against North Korea to help thwart his own lameduck status.
- Korea Telecom has reported an artificial operational loss in an attempt to justify telephone rate hikes scheduled for next month.
- Seoul reaffirms its hard-line stance toward Pyongyang.
